prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

NEW YORK (CNN) -- Topps Meat Co. on Saturday expanded a recall of ground beef from about 300,000  pounds to 21.7 million pounds, one of the largest meat recalls in U.S. history. The recalled products are all ground beef patties with various brand names. In a statement, the Elizabeth, New Jersey, company said the hamburger patties may be contaminated with E. coli O157:H7, a bacterium that can cause severe diarrhea and cramps, as well as other complications. A statement from the U.S. Department of Agriculture said 25 illnesses are under investigation in Connecticut, Florida, Indiana, Maine, New Jersey, New York, Ohio and Pennsylvania. The ground beef products being recalled have a "sell by date" or a "best if used by date" between September 25, 2007, and September 25, 2008, Topps' statement said.  Watch the latest on the beef recall » . The packages also have the marking "Est. 9748" inside the USDA mark of inspection. Tuesday, the company announced a recall of about 331,000 pounds of hamburger meat, according to the USDA. "Because the health and safety of our consumers is our top priority, we are taking these expansive measures," said Vice President of Operations Geoffrey Livermore in the statement. "Topps is continuing to work with the USDA, state departments of health, retailers and distributors to ensure the safety of our consumers. Additionally, we have augmented our internal quality control procedures with microbiologists and food safety experts. We sincerely regret any inconvenience and concerns this may cause our consumers," Livermore said. This is the company's first recall in its 65 years of business, the statement said. Consumers who find the products at home are asked to cut off the UPC code and return it to Topps for a full refund, then dispose of the product immediately, Topps spokeswoman Michelle Williams said. The company said to avoid E. coli, consumers should wash hands thoroughly after handling the beef. Topps set up a toll-free recall help line at (888) 734-0451. Williams said because the products may have been produced up to a year ago, many of them have already been safely consumed. Production in the ground beef area of the company's plant in Elizabeth has been shut down until all the investigations are complete, Williams said in a phone interview. "We're working with the USDA and the CDC [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention] and conducting our own investigation," she added. The products, all ground beef patties and hamburgers with various brand names, were distributed mainly in the northeastern United States, but went to retailers in many other areas of the country as well, Williams said. While the sheer size of the recall is large, two other companies have been involved in larger recalls. In 2002, Pilgrim's Pride recalled more than 27 million pounds of poultry, and Hudson Foods recalled 25 million pounds of ground beef in 1997. E-mail to a friend .

outputs.L1:
**NEW YORK (CNN) —** Topps Meat Co. on Saturday expanded its recall of ground beef from approximately 300,000 pounds to 21.7 million pounds, making it one of the largest meat recalls in U.S. history.

The recalled products consist entirely of ground beef patties sold under various brand names. In a statement, the Elizabeth, New Jersey-based company said the hamburger patties may be contaminated with *E. coli* O157:H7, a bacterium that can cause severe diarrhea, cramps and other complications.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture said 25 illnesses are under investigation in Connecticut, Florida, Indiana, Maine, New Jersey, New York, Ohio and Pennsylvania.

According to Topps, the recalled ground beef products have a “sell by” or “best if used by” date between September 25, 2007, and September 25, 2008. The packages also bear the marking “Est. 9748” inside the USDA inspection mark.

*Watch the latest on the beef recall »*

On Tuesday, the company announced a recall of approximately 331,000 pounds of hamburger meat, according to the USDA.

“Because the health and safety of our consumers is our top priority, we are taking these expansive measures,” Vice President of Operations Geoffrey Livermore said in the statement.

“Topps is continuing to work with the USDA, state departments of health, retailers and distributors to ensure the safety of our consumers. Additionally, we have augmented our internal quality control procedures with microbiologists and food safety experts. We sincerely regret any inconvenience and concerns this may cause our consumers,” Livermore said.

The statement noted that this is the company’s first recall in its 65 years of operation.

Consumers who find the recalled products at home are advised to cut off the UPC code and return it to Topps for a full refund, then dispose of the product immediately, Topps spokeswoman Michelle Williams said. The company also advised consumers to wash their hands thoroughly after handling the beef to avoid *E. coli* contamination.

Topps has established a toll-free recall assistance line at (888) 734-0451.

Williams said that because some of the products may have been produced as long as a year ago, many have already been safely consumed. Production in the ground beef area of the company’s Elizabeth plant has been suspended until all investigations are complete, she said in a telephone interview.

“We’re working with the USDA and the CDC [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention] and conducting our own investigation,” Williams added.

The products—all ground beef patties and hamburgers sold under various brand names—were distributed primarily in the northeastern United States, although they were also shipped to retailers in many other parts of the country, Williams said.

Although the recall is substantial, two other companies have been involved in larger recalls. In 2002, Pilgrim’s Pride recalled more than 27 million pounds of poultry, while Hudson Foods recalled 25 million pounds of ground beef in 1997.

outputs.L2:
NEW YORK (CNN) — Topps Meat Co. increased its ground-beef recall on Saturday from roughly 300,000 pounds to 21.7 million pounds, making it one of the biggest meat recalls ever recorded in the United States.

The affected items consist entirely of ground-beef patties sold under several brand names. Topps, based in Elizabeth, New Jersey, said in a statement that the patties could contain E. coli O157:H7. The bacterium can lead to intense diarrhea, abdominal cramps and additional health complications.

According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, officials are investigating 25 illnesses reported in Connecticut, Florida, Indiana, Maine, New Jersey, New York, Ohio and Pennsylvania.

Topps said the recalled products carry “sell by” or “best if used by” dates ranging from September 25, 2007, through September 25, 2008. The packaging also bears the establishment number “Est. 9748” within the USDA inspection seal.

The company had initially announced on Tuesday that it was recalling approximately 331,000 pounds of hamburger meat, the USDA reported.

Geoffrey Livermore, Topps’ vice president of operations, said the company was taking such broad action because consumer health and safety were its highest priorities. He added that Topps was cooperating with the USDA, state health agencies, retailers and distributors to protect customers. The company had also strengthened its in-house quality-control efforts by bringing in microbiologists and food-safety specialists. Livermore apologized for the worry and disruption the recall might create.

According to the company’s statement, this was Topps’ first recall in its 65-year history.

Topps spokeswoman Michelle Williams advised anyone who has one of the products at home to remove the UPC code and send it to the company for a complete refund, then immediately discard the meat. To reduce the risk of E. coli exposure, the company also recommended washing hands thoroughly after touching the beef.

Topps established a toll-free recall assistance number at (888) 734-0451.

Williams noted that some of the products may have been made as long as a year earlier, meaning many had likely already been eaten without incident. She said in a telephone interview that operations in the ground-beef section of the Elizabeth facility had been suspended and would remain closed until every investigation was finished.

She added that Topps was carrying out its own inquiry while working with both the USDA and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The recalled hamburgers and ground-beef patties, marketed under multiple brand names, were shipped primarily to the northeastern United States, though retailers in numerous other parts of the country also received them, Williams said.

Despite the enormous amount of meat involved, two previous recalls were larger. Pilgrim’s Pride withdrew more than 27 million pounds of poultry in 2002, while Hudson Foods recalled 25 million pounds of ground beef in 1997.

outputs.L4:
Topps Meat Co. dramatically expanded its recall of frozen ground beef patties after an investigation found that far more products than initially believed could be contaminated with E. coli O157:H7. The recall grew from roughly 300,000 pounds to 21.7 million pounds, making it one of the largest meat recalls in U.S. history.

The company took the action while working with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service, retailers, distributors, and independent food-safety experts. Investigators sought to determine the source and scope of the contamination while tracing shipments and removing affected packages from stores and other distribution channels.

The recalled products were produced over several months and sold under the Topps name and a variety of other labels. Packages carried the establishment number “EST. 9748” inside the USDA inspection mark. Because the patties were frozen, officials warned that consumers might still have them in home freezers even after retailers removed the products from shelves.

At the time of the expanded recall, health authorities were investigating 25 illnesses in eight states that could be associated with the meat. E. coli O157:H7 can cause severe abdominal cramps and bloody diarrhea. In some cases—particularly among children, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems—the infection can lead to serious complications, including kidney failure.

Consumers were urged to check their freezers carefully and not eat any recalled patties. Affected products should be discarded or returned to the place of purchase for a refund. Officials also advised consumers to prevent raw meat and its juices from coming into contact with other foods, utensils, or kitchen surfaces.

Although thorough cooking can kill E. coli, regulators emphasized that recalled products should not be consumed. The size of the action reflected both the broad distribution of the patties and the difficulty of determining which individual packages might have been contaminated. Topps said it would continue cooperating with authorities and retailers to ensure that all affected products were identified and removed as quickly as possible.
